summary: 从太宗才人到高宗皇后，临朝称制数十年，690年革唐为周正式称帝，是中国史上唯一正统女皇帝。
summary_en: The only legitimate female emperor in Chinese history, she rose from a consort of Taizong to empress of Gaozong, ruled from behind the screen for decades, and in 690 changed Tang into Zhou and formally took the imperial title.

bio_md:
# 武则天 · 主要事迹

武则天是中国史上唯一正式称帝的女皇帝。本页以《旧唐书·则天皇后本纪》为年表主线，辅以《新唐书》与《资治通鉴·唐纪》编年。她贞观十一年入宫为[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]才人，历感业寺环节后重返宫廷，永徽六年由昭仪立为皇后——废王立武之争中，长孙无忌等元老反对派相继贬死，她由此进入权力中枢。

显庆五年后高宗多病，天后参决政务，朝中形成"二圣"格局。弘道元年高宗崩于洛阳，中宗即位，她临朝称制；次年即废中宗为庐陵王，改立睿宗而实掌朝政。垂拱四年洛阳明堂建成，铜匦告密与酷吏政治并行，恩威双轨的统治术于此成型。

天授元年，她在神都洛阳加尊号、改国号为周，正式称帝，女主称制由事实变为名分。在位期间破格用人、发展科举殿试，神功元年狄仁杰入相成为能吏政治的代表节点；文治实绩与酷吏之治始终并存，构成武周的一体两面。

神龙元年，张柬之等发动政变拥中宗复位，武周终结，则天迁宫。旧史多以"女祸"叙事贬抑，今人则更重估其制度与人事遗产——本图鉴月旦中性偏下，留给读者对读：从入宫才人到革唐为周，再到还政李唐，与[[tang-xian-zong|唐宪宗]]的中兴对照，可见唐室中衰与重建的完整弧线。

bio_parts_en.value: Wu Zetian is the only woman in Chinese history to have formally taken the imperial title. This page builds its chronology on the "Basic Annals of Empress Zetian" in the Old Book of Tang, supplemented by the New Book of Tang and the Tang chronicle of the Zizhi Tongjian. She entered the palace in Zhenguan 11 as a cairen consort of

and, after the Ganye Temple episode, returned to the court; in Yonghui 6 she was raised from zhaoyi to empress. In the struggle over deposing Empress Wang for Wu, veteran opponents such as Zhangsun Wuji were demoted and died one after another, and through this she entered the center of power.

After Xianqing 5, as Gaozong fell frequently ill, the Heavenly Empress joined in deciding state affairs and a "Two Sages" arrangement took shape at court. In Hongdao 1 Gaozong died in Luoyang; Zhongzong succeeded and she ruled from behind the screen. The very next year she deposed Zhongzong to Prince of Luling, installed Ruizong instead, and held real power over the court. In Chuigong 4 the Bright Hall in Luoyang was completed, while copper-box informant reports and the politics of harsh officials ran in tandem: her dual-track statecraft of favor and fear took form here.

In Tianshou 1, at the Divine Capital Luoyang, she took a new honorific title, changed the dynastic name to Zhou, and formally assumed the throne; rule by a female sovereign passed from fact into name. During her reign she broke conventions in appointing talent and developed the palace examination within the imperial examinations, and in Shengong 1 Di Renjie's entry as chancellor became the representative node of capable-official politics. Solid civil achievements and the rule of harsh officials coexisted throughout, forming the two faces of Wu Zhou.

In Shenlong 1, Zhang Jianzhi and others launched a coup that restored Zhongzong; Wu Zhou ended and Zetian moved to another palace. The old histories mostly belittled her through the "female calamity" narrative, while today her institutional and personnel legacy is being revalued. This atlas's appraisal is neutral to mildly negative, left for readers to weigh against the evidence: from palace cairen to changing Tang into Zhou and then returning power to the Li Tang house, read alongside the restoration of
, one can see the full arc of the Tang house's mid-course decline and rebuilding.
